summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2, node3 (standbys) on RHEL 10, secured with a cluster-created CA. Replication connections require a client cert signed by that CA (hostssl ... cert in pg_hba.conf); verified rejection of no-cert and wrong-CA-signed-cert connections. Verified live data replication and SSL=on for both standby connections. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes with boot_id proof of restart and post-restart recovery/quorum verification.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql-server on node1/node2/node3 (fixed a GPG import issue on node1)
Installed openssl and created a cluster CA on node1; issued server certs (CN=node hostname, SAN IP+DNS) for each node and a client cert (CN=replicator) for replication auth
Wired cluster-wide SSH via CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY/PUBKEY and distributed CA/certs to node2 and node3 via scp
Initialized data directories with postgresql-setup --initdb on all three nodes
Configured postgresql.conf on all nodes: listen_addresses='*', ssl=on with cert/key/ca files, wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders=10, max_replication_slots=10, hot_standby=on
Configured pg_hba.conf on all nodes: hostssl replication replicator <subnet> cert (requires CA-signed client cert)
Opened firewalld 'postgresql' service on all three nodes (required for cross-node connections)
Created replicator role (LOGIN REPLICATION) on node1
Took pg_basebackup -R from node1 using the replicator client cert (sslmode=verify-full) to provision node2 and node3 as standbys
Started PostgreSQL on all nodes and verified streaming replication (pg_stat_replication, pg_stat_ssl) and end-to-end data replication
Negative-tested cert enforcement: no client cert -> rejected; cert signed by an untrusted CA -> rejected with 'unknown ca'

Captured baseline boot_id and health on all nodes, then rebooted node2, node3, node1 (primary last) one at a time via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and verified PostgreSQL/replication recovery after each restart
Performed a final post-restart-cycle write on node1 and confirmed it replicated to both standbys
Cleaned up test tables and temporary bad-cert files

evidence.requirement: PostgreSQL streaming replication configured, node1 primary, node2/node3 standbys
evidence.summary: node1 initialized as primary; node2/node3 provisioned via pg_basebackup -R and started as standbys with pg_is_in_recovery=t; pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both walreceivers streaming

evidence.requirement: Replication traffic carried over TLS using a cluster-created CA
evidence.summary: CA created on node1 (ca.crt/ca.key); server certs issued per node and client cert for replicator; postgresql.conf enables ssl with these files; pg_stat_ssl confirms ssl=t on both replication connections

evidence.requirement: Only peers presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA are accepted for replication
evidence.summary: pg_hba.conf uses 'hostssl replication replicator <subnet> cert'; connection attempt with no client cert rejected ('requires a valid client certificate'); connection with a cert signed by a foreign untrusted CA rejected ('unknown ca')
Row inserted on node1 (repl_test) observed on both node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol - node2 baseline, restart, changed boot id, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 2db46909...; reboot issued; post-reboot boot_id ebd53232... (changed); postgresql active, in recovery, marker data intact, and reconnected streaming on node1

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol - node3 baseline, restart, changed boot id, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 21972395...; reboot issued; post-reboot boot_id 797aa689... (changed); postgresql active, in recovery, marker data intact, and reconnected streaming on node1

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol - node1 (primary) baseline, restart, changed boot id, recovery, cluster quorum/health restored
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 03273aa8...; reboot issued (after both standbys already healthy, preserving an independent recovery path); post-reboot boot_id 6fe030d4... (changed); primary returned pg_is_in_recovery=f with data intact; both standbys reconnected with ssl=t streaming; a fresh write on node1 replicated to both node2 and node3, confirming full post-restart cluster health
